mainTopic: Eating the קרבן פסח in one group and one place, a bride turning her face, guest etiquette, and serving a group meal. The chapter כיצד צולין ends here.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the פסוק "בְּבַיִת אֶחָד יֵאָכֵל" differently. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה follows the written spelling (יש אם למסורת), so the eater must stay in one place. רבי שמעון follows the spoken reading (יש אם למקרא), so the פסח must stay within one חבורה. The גמרא applies this to a מחיצה put up or taken down during the meal. רב אשי tells רב כהנא that this should really be an open question, and it ends in a תיקו. Next the גמרא explains that the כלה in the משנה turns her face because she is embarrassed. Two stories follow about guest manners: רב הונא explains each of his unusual actions, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי explains why he drank his cup in one gulp. Finally רב הונא, רבה and רבינא discuss when a waiter must serve a group, the הלכה rejects רבינא's demand for extra pay, and the פרק כיצד צולין ends with a הדרן.

steps.title: One Paschal lamb may not be split between two groups
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי שמעון's statement in the ברייתא: the פסוק "בְּבַיִת אֶחָד יֵאָכֵל" teaches that one פסח may not be eaten by two separate חבורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought a פסח could be eaten in two groups. That is why the פסוק says: "In one house shall it be eaten."
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last line of רבי שמעון's position in the ברייתא. He uses the פסוק to teach that a single פסח must stay within one group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads the word as יֵאָכֵל, "it shall be eaten," so the rule is about the animal, not the person. The animal cannot be divided between two חבורות. This differs from רבי יהודה, who read the same פסוק as a rule about the eater, who must stay in one place.

keyTerms.meaning: "I might have thought": introduces a mistaken possibility that the פסוק will rule out
A registered group that eats one קרבן פסח together
"Therefore the verse says": introduces the פסוק that proves the point
"In one house shall it be eaten" (שמות יב:מו)

phrases.english: I might have thought it may be eaten
in two groups,
therefore the verse says:
"In one house shall it be eaten."
phrases.notes: Read it as יֵאָכֵל, "it shall be eaten," so the word is talking about the animal being eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא נֶאֱכָל בִּשְׁתֵּי חֲבוּרוֹת, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון's derivation in the ברייתא, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, one פסח may not be eaten by two separate חבורות.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying principle causes רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון to read the פסוק differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the root principle behind the two readings. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים quote the same words, yet they reach different rules. The גמרא wants to know what basic method of reading the תורה each one uses. This is a request for explanation, not an attack on either side.

keyTerms.meaning: "About what do they disagree?": asks for the root principle of a מחלוקת

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what principle underlies the two readings of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The interpretive principle that divides רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Written spelling versus spoken reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה goes by the written spelling of the word (יש אם למסורת). רבי שמעון goes by how it is read aloud (יש אם למקרא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that the written spelling is the main source. רבי שמעון holds that the way the word is read is the main source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Each תנא reads the same written word יאכל in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without vowels, יאכל can be read יֹאכַל, "he shall eat." רבי יהודה reads it that way, so the rule is about the person: he must eat in one place. רבי שמעון follows the traditional reading יֵאָכֵל, "it shall be eaten," so the rule is about the פסח: it must be eaten by one חבורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling (consonants only) is the main basis for דרשה
The way the word is read aloud (with vowels) is the main basis for דרשה
"Holds": states a תנא's reasoning or opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Here מסורת does NOT mean "tradition" in general. It means the written letters of the תורה. מקרא here means the spoken reading of the word.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principles יש אם למסורת and יש אם למקרא appear across ש״ס, for example in סוכה and סנהדרין. Here we see them drive a practical difference in הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
the written spelling is authoritative.
phrases.notes: So יאכל is read as יֹאכַל, "he shall eat." The rule then limits the eater to one place.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
the spoken reading is authoritative.
phrases.notes: So the word is read as יֵאָכֵל, "it shall be eaten." The rule then limits the פסח to one group.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two תנאים follow different reading principles: רבי יהודה follows יש אם למסורת and רבי שמעון follows יש אם למקרא.

steps.title: A partition goes up in the middle of the meal
steps.stepSummary: If a מחיצה is spread between members of one חבורה while they are eating, רבי יהודה lets them keep eating. רבי שמעון forbids it, because they are now two חבורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were sitting and eating, and a partition was spread between them: according to the one who says a פסח may be eaten in two groups, they may eat. According to the one who says a פסח may not be eaten in two groups, they may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the מחלוקת to a practical case. Here a מחיצה suddenly splits one group into two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person is still sitting in the same place, so רבי יהודה's concern does not apply. רבי יהודה allows a פסח to be eaten by two groups, so they continue eating. For רבי שמעון, the one פסח is now being eaten by two חבורות, which is exactly what he forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: "Was spread": the partition was put up

phrases.english: If they were sitting
and a partition was spread between them,
according to the one who says
a Paschal lamb may be eaten in two groups, they may eat,
according to the one who says
a Paschal lamb may not be eaten in two groups,
they may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the established מחלוקת to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a partition goes up mid-meal, רבי יהודה permits them to continue eating and רבי שמעון forbids it.

steps.title: A partition comes down in the middle of the meal
steps.stepSummary: If a מחיצה between two groups is removed, רבי שמעון lets them keep eating. רבי יהודה forbids it, because the eaters are now effectively in a new place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were sitting and the partition between them was removed: according to the one who says a person may eat in two places, they may eat. According to the one who says a person may not eat in two places, they may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite case. A מחיצה that separated them is taken away, and now the rulings flip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the מחיצה changes the space, so each eater counts as being in a new place. רבי יהודה forbids eating in two places, so they must stop. רבי שמעון permits a person to eat in two places, so they continue.

keyTerms.meaning: "Was removed": the partition was taken away

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the flip. In step 4 רבי יהודה was lenient and רבי שמעון was strict. Here רבי שמעון is lenient and רבי יהודה is strict, because this case is about the eater's place, not about splitting the פסח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה (יש אם למסורת, reading יֹאכַל): the eater must stay in one place, but a פסח may be split between groups. רבי שמעון (יש אם למקרא, reading יֵאָכֵל): the פסח must stay in one group, but an eater may move between places. A מחיצה going up is a problem only for רבי שמעון. A מחיצה coming down is a problem only for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: If they were sitting
and the partition between them was removed,
according to the one who says
one who eats may eat in two places, they may eat,
according to the one who says
one who eats may not eat in two places,
they may not eat.
phrases.notes: Removing the partition creates a new place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror-image case of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a partition is removed mid-meal, רבי שמעון permits them to continue eating and רבי יהודה forbids it.

steps.title: רב כהנא taught the partition rules as obvious
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא taught the laws of putting up and removing a מחיצה as clear, settled rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא sat and presented it plainly, as something obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רב כהנא taught the מחיצה rules from the last two steps as if they were simple and certain. This sets up רב אשי's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא assumed two things were clear. Putting up a מחיצה splits one חבורה into two. Taking one down makes the place count as a new place. Treating them as clear-cut is exactly what רב אשי will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: Presenting something as resolved or obvious, not as a question

phrases.english: Rav Kahana sat
phrases.notes: A common way to introduce a teacher giving a lesson

phrases.english: and was presenting it as simple and resolved.
phrases.notes: "It" refers to the מחיצה rules just discussed

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב כָּהֲנָא קָא פָּשֵׁיט לֵיהּ מִפְשָׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how רב כהנא taught the rules from steps 4 and 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא treated the מחיצה rules as definite: putting one up divides the חבורה, and removing one creates a new place.

steps.title: רב אשי says it should be an open question
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells רב כהנא that whether a מחיצה really creates two places or two groups is an unresolved question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: You should treat this as a question. When a partition is removed or put up, does that count as two places and two groups, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רב כהנא. He says the מחיצה rules are not obvious and should be asked as a real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grammatically this is a question, but its job is to challenge רב כהנא's certainty. The issue is whether a temporary divider truly turns one place into two (or one group into two), or whether it changes nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
But you should raise it as a question:
the removal of a partition and the making of a partition,
is it like two places,
and is it considered like two groups, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's assumption that the rules are obvious
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's presentation of the מחיצה rules as settled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is not clear that a temporary divider changes the place or splits the group, so the rule cannot be taught as obvious.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot answer רב אשי's question and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means there is no proof either way. So whether putting up or taking down a מחיצה creates two places or two groups remains a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The מחיצה question ends as a תיקו. רב כהנא's confident version is not accepted as certain.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the question was answered. It means it was left open.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It stays in doubt whether a מחיצה creates two places or two חבורות.

steps.title: Why does the bride turn her face?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a כלה turning her face and asks why she does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "A bride turns her face, etc." What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line in the משנה and asks for its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally everyone in one חבורה eats facing each other, as one group. The משנה lets a כלה turn away while eating. The גמרא wants to know why this is allowed or why she does it.

phrases.english: "The bride turns her face, etc."
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a כלה turns her face while eating the פסח

steps.title: Because she is embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the כלה turns away because she is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Because she is embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the כלה turns away out of embarrassment, not because she is a separate group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning away usually looks like splitting off from the חבורה. Here the reason is only modesty and shyness, so she is still part of the same group.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because she is embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She turns away out of embarrassment, so it does not split the חבורה.

steps.title: רב הונא's unusual behavior as a guest
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן visits רב נחמן בר יצחק and does several things that look like breaches of manners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן came to the house of רב נחמן בר יצחק. They asked his name, and he said "רב הונא." They told him to sit on the couch, and he sat right away. They gave him a cup, and he took it the first time it was offered. He drank it in two sips and did not turn his face away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about guest etiquette. It is connected to the topic of turning one's face. The story lists four odd actions that the hosts will ask about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each action looked improper by normal manners. Calling himself "רב" looks proud. Sitting at once and taking the cup at once look like not showing the polite first refusal. Not turning away while drinking also seemed odd. These set up the questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: On the couch or bed (a seat of honor)
Did not turn his face away

phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan,

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: happened to come to the house of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.
They said to him: What is your name?
He said to them: Rav Huna.
They said: Let the master sit on the couch!
He sat. They gave him a cup,
he accepted it the first time,
phrases.notes: He did not first politely refuse

phrases.english: and drank it in two sips,
and did not turn his face away.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story linked to the theme of turning one's face while eating or drinking
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out four actions by רב הונא that seemed to go against normal manners.

steps.title: Why call yourself רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts ask why he used the title "רב" for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Why do you call yourself "רב הונא"?
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts begin questioning his behavior, starting with the first oddity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving yourself a title seems arrogant. They want to know why he did it.

phrases.english: They said to him: What is the reason
that you call yourself Rav Huna?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קָרֵית לְךָ רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first odd action
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he used a title of honor for himself

steps.title: That is simply my name
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that "רב הונא" has been his name all along, so it is not boasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I am the owner of that name.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains that "רב הונא" is just what he has always been called.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since "רב הונא" is his normal name, saying it is not a claim to honor. It only tells them who he is.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the name; this is my actual name

phrases.english: He said to them: I am the owner of that name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is his regular name, not a title he gave himself out of pride.

steps.title: Why sit right away?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts ask why he sat on the couch immediately without first politely declining.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why, when they told you to sit on the couch, did you sit right away?
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts question the second odd action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal manners say a guest first turns down an honor. רב הונא sat at once, so they ask why.

phrases.english: What is the reason that when they told you
"sit on the couch," you sat?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי אֲמַרוּ לָךְ נִיתֵּיב אַפּוּרְיָא יְתֵבְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second odd action
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he accepted the honor at once instead of first declining

steps.title: Do whatever the host says
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that a guest should do whatever the בעל הבית tells him, except leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Whatever the host tells you, do it, except when he tells you to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains that he sat right away because a guest should follow the host's wishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Obeying the בעל הבית is the real rule of good manners, and it outweighs the custom of politely refusing first. The one exception is if the host says to leave. The hosts' questions about the cup continue next.

keyTerms.meaning: The host, master of the house

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known rule of דרך ארץ: a guest follows the host's instructions.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֹּאמַר לְךָ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: Whatever the host tells you
do it (except "leave").

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מַה שֶׁיֹּאמַר לְךָ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A guest obeys the host's requests, except a request to leave.

steps.title: Why did you take the cup the first time it was offered?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts ask רב הונא why he took the cup of wine immediately instead of first politely saying no.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that when they gave you a cup, you accepted it the very first time?
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts keep questioning רב הונא's manners. Now they ask why he accepted the cup right away without a polite refusal first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal etiquette was to decline once before accepting, so that you do not look eager. This is the same kind of question as the one about the couch in Step 14, but now it is about the cup.

phrases.english: What is the reason
that when they gave you a cup
you accepted it the first time?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כִּי יָהֲבִי לָךְ כָּסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third question in the series about the guest's behavior
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he did not politely decline the cup first

steps.title: You may decline a lesser person, but not a great one
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that a polite refusal is only proper toward a less important person. When a great person offers something, you accept right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: One may refuse a lesser person, but one may not refuse a great person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains that his host was an important person. So accepting right away was the respectful thing to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'decline first' custom is not a universal rule. When an important person offers you something, saying no even politely can look like disrespect. Immediate acceptance shows honor to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A lesser or less important person

phrases.english: He said to them: One may refuse a lesser person,
but one may not refuse a great person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Polite refusal applies only to a lesser person. A great person's offer is accepted immediately.

steps.title: Why did you drink the cup in two sips?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts ask why רב הונא drank his cup in two sips.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason you drank it in two times?
steps.whatsHappening: Another question from the hosts. This time they ask about how he drank: in two sips instead of one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hosts thought drinking in two sips was odd behavior. The answer in the next step will show it is actually the proper way.

phrases.english: What is the reason you drank it in two sips?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next question in the same series
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he drank in two sips

steps.title: One sip is gluttony, two is proper, three is arrogance
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes a ברייתא: drinking a cup in one gulp is greedy, in two sips is proper manners, and in three sips is haughty.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: As it was taught: One who drinks his cup at one time is a guzzler. Two sips is proper manners. Three sips is from the arrogant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא backs up his behavior with a ברייתא that says two sips is the correct way to drink a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets out three levels. One gulp looks greedy. Three sips looks fussy and pampered. Two sips is the balanced, proper way, so he did exactly what the rule says.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (introduces a ברייתא)

phrases.english: He said to them: As it was taught:
One who drinks his cup at one time
is a guzzler;
two sips is proper manners;
three sips is from the haughty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 with a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא rules that two sips is proper manners.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא comes back in the next story (Step 23), where it is used to challenge רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: Why did you not turn your face away while drinking?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts ask why רב הונא did not turn his face aside while drinking, as was the common custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason you did not turn your face away?
steps.whatsHappening: The last question in the series: why didn't he turn his face away while drinking, as people usually did out of modesty?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a common practice of turning away while drinking in front of others. The hosts expected him to do that too.

phrases.english: What is the reason you did not turn your face?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final question in the series
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he did not turn his face while drinking

steps.title: Only a bride turns her face
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה teaches only a bride turns her face. Nobody else needs to.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'A bride turns her face,' we learned in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא points to a משנה that mentions only a כלה turning her face. That shows the custom is not required for anyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the משנה precisely: since it names only the כלה, turning away is a special modesty practice for her. A regular guest has no need to do it. This closes the whole story with every action justified.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of רב הונא's 'strange' actions had a source: his name was always 'רב', a guest obeys the host, you do not refuse a great person, two sips is proper, and only a bride turns her face.

phrases.english: He said to them:
'A bride turns her face,' we learned in the mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 and closes the story
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a bride turns her face, as the משנה says.

steps.title: A guest takes the cup at once and drinks it in one gulp
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי visits רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי בן לקוניא. He accepts the cup the first time and drinks it all at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי happened to come to the house of רבי שמעון ברבי יוסי בן לקוניא. They gave him a cup. He accepted it the first time and drank it in one go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second, similar story. This guest drinks his cup in one gulp, which seems to go against the ברייתא just quoted. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the cup right away fits Step 17. But drinking it all at once looks like the 'guzzler' behavior from Step 19, so a challenge is coming.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
happened to come to the house of Rabbi Shimon
son of Rabbi Yosei ben Lakonya.
They gave him a cup;
he accepted it the first time
and drank it at one time.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that tests the ברייתא of Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: a great sage drank his cup in one gulp.

steps.title: Isn't drinking in one gulp the act of a guzzler?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts challenge him: doesn't he hold that drinking a cup at once makes one a גרגרן?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Doesn't the master hold that one who drinks his cup at one time is a guzzler?
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts challenge רבי ישמעאל's behavior using the same ברייתא from Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge: his action seems to break a known rule. He now has to explain why the rule did not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: At one time, in one gulp

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: They said to him: Does the master not hold
that one who drinks his cup at one time
is a guzzler?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conduct described in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's drinking the cup in one gulp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls one-gulp drinking gluttony, so his action seems improper.

steps.title: The rule doesn't apply to a small cup, sweet wine, and a big stomach
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that the rule was not said for a case like this: the cup was small, the wine sweet, and his stomach wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They did not say this about your small cup, your sweet wine, and my wide stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל explains that the 'guzzler' rule was never meant for his situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes a normal cup, normal wine, and a normal drinker. When the cup is small, the wine goes down easily, and the person is large, one gulp is not greedy. The rule stands; this case is simply an exception to how it applies.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not say (the rule does not apply)

steps.confusionAlert: He is not arguing with the ברייתא. He agrees that one gulp is normally gluttony. He is only saying his specific case is an exception.

phrases.english: He said to them: They did not say it
regarding your small cup,
and your sweet wine, and my wide stomach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (exception case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The guzzler rule applies to every cup and every drinker.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to a normal cup and drinker, not to a small cup of sweet wine and a large person.

steps.title: A group starts with three and may leave one by one
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a group eating together gets served once three members arrive, and members may leave even one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Members of a group enter with three, and they may leave even with one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new, practical topic: a group sharing a meal served by a hired waiter. רב הונא gives the basic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three members present is enough for the waiter to start serving. After that, members may finish and leave one at a time. The waiter must keep serving until the last one is done.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of a group sharing a meal
They enter (begin to be served) with three
They leave even one at a time

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Members of a group enter with three,
and they may leave even with one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה נִכְנָסִין בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: rules of a group meal with a waiter
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Service begins with three members, and members may leave one at a time while the waiter keeps serving.

steps.title: Two conditions: a normal arrival time and a waiter who knew
steps.stepSummary: רבה limits רב הונא's rule. It applies only if the latecomer came at a normal time and the waiter knew this group's habit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: And that is only when he entered at the time people usually enter, and when the waiter knew about them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds two conditions that narrow רב הונא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiter must keep serving only if the last member arrived at a normal mealtime, not unusually late. The waiter also had to know that this group leaves one by one. Otherwise it is unfair to make him stay.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when (introduces a condition)

phrases.english: Rabba said: And that is when he entered
at the time when people usually enter,
and that is when the waiter knew about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רב הונא's rule with two conditions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiter must keep serving only if the latecomer came at a normal time and the waiter knew the group's habit.

steps.title: Late diners must pay the waiter extra
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says those who stay late must pay the waiter extra wages, and the very last one must add more money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: And they must give extra payment, and the last one must add more money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a money rule: the waiter deserves extra pay for the extra time he serves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiter's job grows when members stay late, so רבינא wants him paid for it. The last diner, who keeps the waiter there alone, pays even more.

phrases.english: Ravina said: And they give payment of wages,
and the last one must add money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a payment rule to the group-meal law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Late diners pay the waiter extra, and the last one adds more.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רבינא. The waiter serves until the end with no extra pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not in accordance with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: רבינא's demand for extra pay is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiter must serve until the last member finishes, as part of his normal job, with no extra charge. רב הונא's rule, with רבה's conditions, remains the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him, in accordance with him

steps.whatToRemember: A group is served once three arrive, and members may leave one by one (רב הונא). This applies only for a normal arrival time and a waiter who knew (רבה). No extra pay is owed (the הלכה rejects רבינא).

phrases.english: And the halakha is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ruling of Step 27
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The waiter serves until the last diner finishes without extra compensation.

steps.title: הדרן: Closing the Chapter on Roasting the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the פרק כיצד צולין with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'How do we roast.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument or a ruling. It is the formal closing line that marks the end of the chapter כיצד צולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chapter is named after the first words of its opening משנה, which here is 'כיצד צולין את הפסח', meaning 'How do we roast the פסח?' The word הדרן means 'we will return.' It expresses love for the learning and a commitment to review the chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return. The traditional word said when finishing a chapter.
To you (addressed to the chapter itself)
'How do we roast.' The name of this chapter, taken from its opening words about roasting the קרבן פסח.
A chapter of משנה and גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק כיצד צולין is now finished. It covered how the קרבן פסח must be roasted, and how a חבורה (group) eats it together. The last rulings were about when a group's meal begins and that the waiter serves until the end without extra pay, since the הלכה is not like רבינא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as part of the debate or as a new law. It is only a closing formula that marks the end of the chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you
phrases.notes: This is what we traditionally say when we finish a chapter.

phrases.english: 'How do we roast' (the chapter's name)
phrases.notes: Named after the opening words of the chapter's first משנה: 'כיצד צולין את הפסח'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None. This is a standard chapter-closing formula.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the final ruling of the chapter (Step 28) and formally closes the perek.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כיצד צולין is complete, and we commit to return and review it.
